title: Preschool Expansion Grants
before:
Pre-Kindergarten Expansion Grants

The first years of life are a critical developmental time in forming the basis for learning and social interaction. Investments in early learning have powerful long-term paybacks. The pandemic heightened the difficulty that many Maine parents and caregivers already faced in struggling to locate pre-kindergarten or child care. Access gaps are especially acute in Maine's rural communities. The Maine Jobs and Recovery Plan committed $10 million dollars to address these access gaps.

The Maine Department of Education has helped schools increase the number of children accessing high-quality pre-kindergarten by offering funds to establish or expand public pre-k programs. Through multiple competitive grant rounds, the department has provided funding to local school administrative units (SAUs) to cover facility renovations, staff recruitment and training, and other start-up costs linked to establishing new public pre-kindergarten programs, expanding to additional classrooms, or transitioning from part-day/part-week to full-day/full-week. Priority has been given to schools that partner with community programs such as Head Start or child care, provide a longer duration of education, and serve socioeconomically disadvantaged students. The department has and will continue to provide technical assistance and professional learning to SAUs for pre-kindergarten expansion.

Grant Funds from Maine Jobs and Recovery Plan (2021–2026)

Four rounds of grant opportunities were offered to SAUs to start or expand pre-k in the 2022–23, 2023–24, 2024–25, and 2025–26 school years. Grantees for each round can be viewed in the expandable sections below. Each chart indicates the model of each SAU's pre-k program, enrollment (actual and projected), community partners, and funding awarded to date.

For any questions regarding the Pre-K Expansion Grant, please contact Lee Anne Larsen at leeanne.larsen@maine.gov.

decisions.label: Write the email addresses the same way
decisions.why: 2 addresses are shown in whatever case it was typed in. The house form capitalises each name and leaves a middle initial in lower case — leeanne.larsen@maine.gov → Leeanne.Larsen@maine.gov. Only the first letter of each part changes, so a name that spells itself LaBreck keeps doing so.

decisions.label: Let a lone card use the full width
decisions.why: 1 row holds a single card in a part-width column, so it takes a third or a half of the page and the rest is blank. A row of one is not a grid.

decisions.label: Make a loose address look like an address
decisions.why: 1 email address sits in the body of this page rather than in a contact block, drawn exactly like every other link — so the one that opens a mail window looks the same as the ones that go to web pages. The chip carries the same envelope the banner's contact link uses. The address itself does not change.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.

decisions.label: Make a bold line a heading
decisions.why: "FY 2022–24 School Year" → "2022-2024 School Year", and a heading rather than a bold paragraph. A heading names a section; it does not introduce one in a sentence, so the sentence and its colon come off.

decisions.label: Make a bold line a heading
decisions.why: "FY 2023–24 and 2024–25 School Years" → "2023-2024 & 2024-2025 School Year", and a heading rather than a bold paragraph. A heading names a section; it does not introduce one in a sentence, so the sentence and its colon come off.

decisions.label: Make a bold line a heading
decisions.why: "FY 2025–26 School Year" → "2025-2026 School Year", and a heading rather than a bold paragraph. A heading names a section; it does not introduce one in a sentence, so the sentence and its colon come off.

decisions.label: Let a column of short entries keep them on one line
decisions.why: 11 columns hold nothing longer than sixteen characters and sit in a table that also has a column of paragraphs. The layout sizes a column by its longest unbreakable run, so "Step 1" asks only for the width of "Step" and the paragraph column takes the rest — which is how "Step" and "1" end up on separate lines in a column with room to spare beside it. Held on one line, the column asks for what it needs. Nothing is widened by force and no word changes.

decisions.label: Add a contents list (3 sections)
decisions.why: Built from the section headings already on the page. Below three sections a list is not a route.
